release_scope: ForgeHarness 0.4.0 candidate: public durable scoped sessions (plan phase S1) over SDK API v1, single-machine POSIX/local SQLite and trusted host adapters
verification_time_note: Command timestamps, logs and per-attempt reports are preserved under reports/session-verification/; the source profile ran in the repository and the clean profile reran every gate on a hash-checked copy of the frozen inputs.
review_method: Maintainer-style self-review, contract/fault regressions, frozen candidate and clean checkout-equivalent rerun plus minimal wheel install; no independent external certification and no real-model or business-quality evaluation
source_kind: archive checkout equivalent; no Git metadata
implemented: Embeddable SessionService over the public Harness and WorkflowRunner: sessions fixed to application, policy version, tenant, actor, resources and workspace; ordered turns with stable request keys; host re-authorization on every operation
Bounded untrusted conversation history assembled through the existing context compiler; recorded source versions; actual model input remains the trace's model.request evidence
Per-session single writer, one active turn at a time, crash reconciliation on the stable run id, and explicit failure/exhaustion/awaiting-approval/success states
Delegated approval with a separately authenticated approver and single-use grants; a consumed or inapplicable grant is refused rather than acknowledged
Evidence transformation before persistence, deletion tombstones, retired session identities and local copy cleanup
Optional FastAPI session router kept out of the base SDK and wheel; synthetic legal-style and commerce-style client with restart, replay, revocation and cross-tenant refusal
Candidate-bound verification gate: source freeze that refuses to overwrite, clean-copy rerun, wheel/sdist membership against the freeze, minimal wheel-only install

source.model_profile: keyless scripted; synthetic token usage; no live-model, legal accuracy, business outcome or cost claim

clean.model_profile: keyless scripted; synthetic token usage; no live-model, legal accuracy, business outcome or cost claim

verification.clean_copy: Every frozen input copied and hash-checked into a report-local working tree; full gates rerun in a fresh Python 3.12 environment.
verification.minimal_consumer: Wheel-only fresh environment outside the repository: imports without FastAPI or LangGraph and runs all three public examples.
verification.dependency_audit: pip-audit over the exported requirements: no unignored finding in either scope. The accepted PYSEC-2026-3740 (transitive, optional frameworks extra) is passed as --ignore-vuln and remains an accepted residual risk (docs/review FH-019), reachable only through the optional LlamaIndex comparison.

findings.resolution: Replaying a consumed approval grant on a finished turn returned a silent success; it is now refused as a conflict (409). The durable ledger still rejects double consumption. tests/unit/test_session_control.py::test_http_delegated_approval_reauthenticates_and_restarts
Recreating a deleted session identity reported a naming conflict; it is now unavailable (403) and the identity stays retired. tests/unit/test_sessions.py::test_deleted_session_retires_its_identity
The verification driver discarded its failure summary when the source tree could no longer be hashed. tests/unit/test_session_verification.py::test_driver_exception_persists_failed_result

The gate invoked Ruff with --exclude reports, which replaces Ruff's default excludes and linted the whole virtual environment (about 96k findings), so the lint gate could not pass; switched to --extend-exclude plus a project-level reports/ exclusion.

The new session code had never been formatted or linted and benchmarks/ was not importable, so the verification test module failed collection; formatted, linted, packaged and given a pytest pythonpath entry.
README and the scope document advertised SessionService as public SDK while it was not exported; the session types are now exported from forgeharness.sdk and the optional router deliberately is not.

The architecture test's optional-adapter exemption was widened safely: per-module exemption plus assertions that adapters declare their platform dependency and that importing forgeharness loads no optional platform package.
Stale documentation (BUSINESS_MODULES session claim, SDK_GUIDE release version and missing session router section) corrected for the 0.4.0 candidate.

A workflow node adapter failure left the turn looking unstarted instead of recording the durable workflow state and its error; the suspended state is now recorded and the original turn is resumed. tests/unit/test_sessions.py::test_workflow_adapter_failure_does_not_lose_durable_state

The sdist ships the packaging tool's default .gitignore, which was outside the frozen identity, so the 'every sdist member is frozen' rule could never pass. .gitignore is now part of the content-addressed identity (absent root files simply do not contribute; deleting one still changes the digest) instead of being exempted.

not_closed: FH-019 accepted advisory (optional frameworks extra NLTK)
